title: Portal2Bench: Can AI agents solve Portal 2?
excerpt: Can AI agents solve Portal 2? GPT-6.1 Sol solves 20 of 26 test chambers and GPT-6 Astra solves 20, each within $30 and 300 plans.
content_html:
Portal2Bench measures whether AI agents can solve Portal 2's test chambers. Each chamber is a fresh, independent run, scored solved only if the agent finishes within $30 and 300 plans.

Can AI agents solve Portal 2?

Yes. GPT-6.1 Sol (Codex) solves 20 of 26 Portal 2 test chambers. GPT-6 Astra (Codex) solves 20, GPT-6.1 Terra (Codex) 19, Opus 5.5 (Claude Code) 11, Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Code) 6, GPT-6 Luna (Codex) 0 and Fable 5.1 (Claude Code) 3 of 15 so far.

How does Portal2Bench work?

Portal2Bench pauses Portal 2 while the model thinks. The agent sends keys and view turns, and gets back screenshots and its position. It has a notes folder, but no shell, web or console. Each chamber is a fresh run, solved if the agent reaches the next map within 300 plans and $30. 26 chambers from chapters 2 to 5 count. Each model runs in its own harness at its highest effort.

What does a run cost?

Portal2Bench prices each run at API list prices. A solved chamber's median cost runs from $0.74 (GPT-6.1 Terra) to $13.12 (Fable 5.1).

Can the agent cheat?

No. The agent has no shell or web, and its file tools reach only its own notes folder. A QA check flags anything else.

What happens when the agent dies?

The agent respawns at its last checkpoint, as in normal play, and is told only that it died.

Is Portal2Bench made by Valve?

No. Portal2Bench is not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve.
